newsitem.title: USA: Calif. transit agency accepts rail project terms.
newsitem.headline: Calif. transit agency accepts rail project terms.

text.p: Northern California's Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District on Thursday said it agreed to the economic terms set by the airline industry for funding a portion of a San Francisco airport rail project.

BART said it agreed to make an annual payment to the San Francisco International Airport of $2.5 million over the 50-year life of the project. In addition, BART said it agreed to provide airline employees with certain discounts.

"After difficult negotiations, our agreement to make an annual payment for this project and offer an employee discount should close the deal," BART Board President Margaret Pryor said. "We have satisfied all remaining concerns of the airlines over their financial contribution to this project."
The San Francisco International Airport had previously committed $200 million toward the $1.167 billion cost of the 8.7-mile BART rail extension project.
The airport contribution to construction costs would come from airline landing fees and other airport revenues, but the airlines resisted paying the full amount set by the airport.
With the annual payment by BART and other changes agreed to by the airport, the airlines' share of the project cost will drop to $113 million, BART said.
